text:
mia: Heads up — we started seeing 3x token latency / 40% throughput drop on some Dedicated clusters after the driver + kernel roll yesterday. Initial root cause looks like NCCL is falling back to NET/Socket instead of using NVLink/SHM on mixed-sku racks.

owen: What region / pool? Any node lists?

mia: eu-west-1, pool: gpu-pool-2, racks g2/g3. Example node mix: H100 (NVSwitch), A100-SXM, A100-PCIE. Job placements that span those mixed nodes are the ones affected.

sasha: We saw a similar blip in prod-east-1 but assumed it was an infra glitch. Logs I grabbed show NCCL doing p2p discovery then disabling SHM and picking NET.

mia: paste of nvidia-smi topo -m from one of the problematic nodes:
```
       GPU0    GPU1    GPU2    GPU3    CPU Affinity
GPU0     X      NV1     PHB     PHB      0-63
GPU1    NV1      X      PHB     PHB      0-63
GPU2    PHB     PHB      X      PCIe     0-63
GPU3    PHB     PHB     PCIe      X      0-63
```
(so NVLink between GPU0/1, others over PCIe)

mia: NCCL log snippet: 
```
[NCCL WARN] p2p : Peer discovery mismatch across nodes, nvlink path inconsistent
[NCCL INFO] p2p : checking SHM availability
[NCCL WARN] shmem : SHM disabled (mmap/numa mismatch)
[NCCL INFO] transport : falling back to NET/Socket
```

owen: That "mmap/numa mismatch" ring a bell. We recently picked up a kernel build (6.4.x) + NVIDIA driver 545 on a subset of hosts while others stayed on 535. Could be driver/kernel/cuda combo breaking p2p feature detection.

raj: Agreed — nvlink peer discovery has been sensitive to driver vs kernel mismatches historically. Two quick workarounds: 1) constrain critical jobs to homogeneous racks (same SKU + driver), or 2) force a fallback policy in the scheduler to avoid cross-sku placements while we debug.

karen: Can we toggle any NCCL env to gather better traces before rollback?

mia: I enabled: `export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO; export NCCL_TOPO_DUMP_FILE=/tmp/nccl_topo.log` and re-ran a small repro. Logs show inconsistent topology across the two nodes in the same ring — one reports NVLink+SHM, the other reports SHM disabled.

raj: For repro steps I used a 2-node rank test with one H100 + one A100-PCIE and ran `nccl-tests/all_reduce` with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`. Repro was consistent when the host with newer driver/kernel was involved.

sasha: Any sign of PCI BAR or IOMMU differences? We did have a packaging change that flipped iommu=pt on some hosts during the kernel bump. That can affect mmap/NIC registration and therefore SHM.

mia: IOMMU flags differ, yes. Node-123 (new kernel) has `intel_iommu=on` set via cloud-init, Node-124 doesn't.

owen: OK that explains mmap failures. If IOMMU is blocking SHM, NCCL will treat SHM as unsafe and choose NET. But the weird bit is it only happens in mixed racks — when all nodes have the same iommu state + driver it works.

raj: Short term plan: 1) Pin urgent workloads to homogeneous nodes (sched change), 2) Revert kernel on a small canary rack to confirm, 3) Add a detection job that runs `nvidia-smi topo -m` + `dmesg | grep -i iommu` across nodes and flags mismatches.

karen: For the scheduler change I'm opening a placement policy PR to prefer same-sku. If we confirm it's kernel+driver+iommu combo, we should add a preflight check during node onboarding.

mia: Can someone run a controlled rollback on one affected rack and run the all_reduce repro? If rollback restores NVLink/SHM, we'll schedule a full rollback for the rest of mixed racks.

owen: I'll coordinate rollback for rack g2-11 tomorrow during low-traffic window and run the repro. I'll post results here.

infra-bot: Alert: job queue latency for gpu-pool-2 increased by 210% starting 2026-11-14T21:12:03Z — affected jobs: 78 (mixed-node placements)

mia: Thanks. If rollback doesn't fix it we may need to pin driver versions across the fleet or disable `intel_iommu` until we get a proper kernel+driver patch. Also we should add a validation step to our upgrade playbook to check NCCL p2p detection on representative mixed templates.

owen: Update: rolled back rack g2-11 to driver 535 + kernel 6.1 on the canary. Repro now shows SHM available and NCCL uses NVLink — throughput back to expected. I'll schedule the wider rollback after engineering sign-off.

raj: Good repro. We'll also open a vendor ticket (NVIDIA) with the kernel/driver/iommu matrix and attach the nccl debug logs and topo dumps.

mia: Thanks all — keeping this thread as the single place for rollback coordination and vendor ticket updates.
